issues.title: Off-by-one error in scroll index calculation
issues.description: The scroll position calculation uses `state.tabs.count` instead of `state.tabs.count - 1` when scrolling to the last tab. Since array indices are zero-based, accessing index equal to the count will cause an index out-of-bounds crash. This occurs when switching between normal and private tab panels when there's no selected tab, causing the app to attempt scrolling to a non-existent tab position. The original code correctly used `count - 1` to get the last valid index before the inactive tabs feature was removed.

issues.title: Incorrect section index after inactive tabs removal
issues.description: The scrollToTab method hardcodes section index as 1, which was correct when there were two sections (inactive tabs at section 0 and regular tabs at section 1). After removing inactive tabs, there is only one section (section 0), so this will cause scroll operations to fail or crash when trying to access a non-existent section. This affects all scroll-to-tab functionality including selecting tabs, undoing tab closures, and panel switching. The TabDisplayDiffableDataSource now only creates a single section `.tabs`, but this scroll method wasn't updated accordingly.

issues.title: Nested struct added without explicit access control modifier
issues.description: The newly added nested type `v147` is declared as `struct v147` without an explicit access control modifier (e.g., `public`/`internal`/`private`). Rule 11 requires explicit access control on declarations based on intended scope. Many other nested structs in this file use `public struct ...`, so this is an inconsistency and a clear violation in the added code.
issues.rule_name: Rule 11: Properties and Methods Must Have Appropriate Access Control

pr.title: Remove FXIOS-14327 [Clean up] Inactive tabs removal part 2 (final)

structured_output.summary:
This PR finishes removing the Inactive Tabs feature from the tab tray. It deletes the InactiveTabs cells, header/footer views, section manager and model, strips the inactive-tab actions, toasts, state fields and reducer branches, and collapses the tab collection view from two sections to one. The project file, accessibility identifiers, XCUI screen graph and tests are updated to match. The cleanup is mostly thorough and internally consistent.

The removal is not complete. Collapsing to a single section left three call sites still assuming the old layout. `TabDisplayView.scrollToTab` hardcodes `section: 1`, which the new `isValid(indexPath:)` guard rejects, so scroll-to-selected-tab and scroll-to-tab silently stop working. The "no selected tab, scroll to bottom" branch now returns `tabs.count` instead of `tabs.count - 1`, which is out of range and is asserted against by an unchanged test. And `TabTrayStateTests.swift` still references the deleted `TabPanelMiddlewareActionType.refreshInactiveTabs`, so the ClientTests target will not compile. These need fixing before merge.

architecture.overview:
The tab tray is driven by a Redux-style store. `TabManagerMiddleware` builds a `TabDisplayModel` from `TabManager`, and `TabsPanelState` reduces middleware and view actions into the state that `TabDisplayView` renders through `TabDisplayDiffableDataSource`. Before this PR, the collection view had two sections: an optional Inactive Tabs section (section 0) and the regular tabs section (section 1). Scrolling used the section index to locate the target cell.

This PR removes the inactive section end to end. The collection now has a single `.tabs` section, so `TabDisplayView` no longer needs section-aware layout or supplementary views, and `ScrollState` no longer carries an `isInactiveTabSection` flag. The view layer still assumes section 1 for scrolling, and the bottom-of-list index changed, so the scroll path is where the cleanup is incomplete.
steps: Entry point: `TabManagerMiddleware` handles `TabPanelViewAction`s (select, close, undo) and dispatches `TabPanelMiddlewareAction`s carrying a `TabDisplayModel`. Inactive-tab branches and helpers are removed here.

Reducer: `TabsPanelState` reduces middleware actions into `tabs`, `scrollState` and `isPrivateMode`. `createTabScrollBehavior` now returns a `ScrollState` with only `toIndex` and `withAnimation`, and its bottom-of-list index changed from `count - 1` to `count`.

View: `TabDisplayDiffableDataSource.updateSnapshot` builds one `.tabs` section. `TabDisplayView.createLayout` always returns the tabs layout, and the header/footer supplementary views and inactive cell are deleted.
Scrolling: `TabDisplayView.scrollToTab` builds an `IndexPath` from `scrollState.toIndex` with a hardcoded `section: 1`. That section no longer exists, so the `isValid` guard drops the scroll.

Tests and project: XCUI identifiers move from `_1_x` to `_0_x`, the screen graph drops the inactive toggle, and the pbxproj removes the deleted files. `TabTrayStateTests` still references the removed `refreshInactiveTabs` case.

diagrams.description: Shows how tab data moves from TabManager through the middleware and reducer into the single-section collection view, including the scroll path that still hardcodes section 1.

structured_output.verdictRationale: The ClientTests target won't compile because `TabTrayStateTests` still references the removed `.refreshInactiveTabs` case. Scroll-to-tab is broken at runtime: `scrollToTab` uses a hardcoded section 1 that no longer exists, and the bottom-scroll index is one past the end. The PR's own scroll unit test still expects `tabCount - 1`, so that test fails. These are regressions in core tab tray behavior.

findings.title: Scroll-to-tab uses a hardcoded section that no longer exists
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/Tabs/Views/TabDisplayView.swift`, `scrollToTab(_:)` (around line 172) builds `IndexPath(row: scrollState.toIndex, section: 1)`. After the inactive-tabs removal the tab collection has a single section at index 0, so the path is rejected by `isValid(indexPath:)` and the scroll silently never happens. Change the section to 0 (the tabs section), and check that nothing else in the file still assumes section 1. Match the other tabs-section index usage in the file.

findings.title: Test target won't compile: TabTrayStateTests uses removed refreshInactiveTabs case
findings.body: `TabPanelMiddlewareActionType.refreshInactiveTabs` is removed in this PR (see `TabPanelAction.swift`), but `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests/TabTray/TabTrayStateTests.swift` (`testRefreshInactiveTabsAction`, around line 142) still references it. That test file is not in the diff, so the change is missing from the PR, and the whole ClientTests target fails to build. Every other test in the target is blocked until it's fixed.
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests/TabTray/TabTrayStateTests.swift`, delete `testRefreshInactiveTabsAction` (around line 142). It references `TabPanelMiddlewareActionType.refreshInactiveTabs`, which this PR removes from `TabPanelAction.swift`, so the ClientTests target won't compile. Also search the test target for other references to removed inactive-tab symbols (`refreshInactiveTabs`, `InactiveTabsModel`, `toggleInactiveTabs`, `closedAllInactiveTabs`, `isInactiveTab`) and remove them.

findings.title: Bottom-of-list scroll index is now out of range
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/Tabs/State/TabsPanelState.swift`, in `createTabScrollBehavior`, the `scrollToSelectedTab` fallback (around line 143) was changed to `ScrollState(toIndex: state.tabs.count, ...)`. Restore it to `state.tabs.count - 1` so it points to the last tab, as the comment says and as `TabsPanelStateTests.testCreateTabScrollBehavior_forScrollToSelectedTab_noSelectedTab_returnsLastTab_ifTabsNotEmpty` expects. Keep the removal of `isInactiveTabSection` otherwise unchanged.

findings.title: MPL license header removed from TabPanelAction.swift
findings.body:
The first three lines of `TabPanelAction.swift` (the MPL 2.0 header) were deleted in the diff. Sibling files in this area carry the header, so this breaks the project convention and the license notice for the file. It looks unintentional, since nothing else in the PR touches the header.

::diff{file="firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/Tabs/Action/TabPanelAction.swift" lines="1-4"}
findings.fixPrompt: Restore the three-line Mozilla Public License v2.0 header at the top of `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/Tabs/Action/TabPanelAction.swift`, matching the header in sibling files such as `TabDisplayView.swift`. The header was accidentally dropped in this PR.

findings.title: Removed string keys are moved into a version-named struct instead of deleted
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift`, the `struct v147` block near the end of the `String` extension holds Inactive Tabs strings that are no longer used anywhere. Either delete the block (no non-test references remain), or if the keys must stay for localization, add a comment explaining why and make the struct `public` to match its siblings.

findings.title: Clean removal of inactive-tab state, actions and view code
findings.body: Most of the removal is done well. The deleted files are removed from `project.pbxproj`, the state and action types drop their inactive fields together, and the diffable data source and layout branches collapse to a single path. The `shouldHideInactiveTabs` guard is gone, and the tests were updated to match the new `TabDisplayModel` and `TabsPanelState` initializers.
